first.what_it_is: A phone-camera recording of a laptop/monitor screen showing an AI app-builder web IDE in (near) full-screen, with its chat/left panel almost entirely off the left edge of frame and its live preview pane filling the screen. The preview is rendering the `/about` route of a personal academic website for "Korkut Kaynardag, PhD" — a warm ivory, serif-headed, two-column About page. Across the 18 seconds the person does nothing but scroll the preview slowly downward with the mouse wheel: top of the page (title + social links + Biography + portrait + CV button), then the rest of the Biography, then the "At a glance — September 2026" three-number stat band, then the full five-entry "Career timeline", ending with a small scroll back up so the "Career timeline" heading is visible again. No clicks, no menu opening, no typing. The hamburger menu is never opened, so the site's navigation items are never revealed in this clip. Windows taskbar at the bottom reads 10:08 AM, 9/15/2026, keyboard "ENG".
first.app_or_tool: An AI app-builder / "vibe-coding" web IDE in full-screen browser mode (no address bar or tab strip is visible in any frame, so the browser chrome is hidden — the bar at the very top of the screen is the app's own toolbar). Toolbar contents, left to right: a list/panel-toggle icon; a diagonal collapse-arrows icon; a blue-tinted rounded pill with a globe icon reading "Korkut's Research Hub" (the project name); a document/page icon; a `</>` code icon; a layers/stack icon; a gap; a monitor/desktop viewport icon; a circular reload icon; the route path "/about" in bold; a chevron (page/route dropdown); an open-in-new-tab icon; then a dark "Share" pill, a violet-to-purple gradient pill with a lightning bolt reading "Upgrade", and a blue rounded pill reading "Publish". The bottom-left sliver of the hidden left panel shows a rounded chat composer with a microphone icon and a circular up-arrow (send) button, i.e. an AI chat panel. This combination — project pill + preview/code/layers switcher + device toggle + route path + Share/Upgrade/Publish + AI chat composer — matches Lovable (lovable.dev) most closely; Lovable is my best identification. What is certain from the pixels: it is NOT Wix (no Wix editor left rail, no Wix top bar with site menu/Preview, no Wix chrome), NOT Word or PowerPoint (no ribbon, no slide rail, no document page frame), and NOT Claude Artifacts (Artifacts has no `/route` path field, no project pill, and no Share+Upgrade+Publish trio). A Figma Make / Bolt / v0-style builder cannot be excluded with 100% certainty at this camera resolution, but v0 and Bolt label the right-hand action "Deploy", not "Publish", which argues against them. The site being previewed is a client-routed multi-page app (route `/about`), not a static single artifact.

Biography

I received my bachelor's and master's degrees from the Department of Civil Engineering at Boğaziçi University in 2013 and 2016, respectively, and my Ph.D. from the Department of Civil Engineering at The University of Texas at Austin in 2023.

I served as a project assistant at Boğaziçi University from 2013 to 2014 and as a research assistant from 2014 to 2016, followed by a graduate research assistantship at The University of Texas at Austin from 2016 to 2023. After completing my doctorate, I continued my career in the United States as an Applied Data Scientist at Transtek International Group (2023–2024) and as a Senior AI Engineer at Renesas Electronics America (2024–2026).

Since August 27, 2026, I have served as an Assistant Professor in the Department of Civil Engineering at Izmir Institute of Technology, where my research focuses on structural health monitoring, nondestructive damage detection, smart sensors, and smart cities.

Over my career I have worked on tall buildings, masonry buildings and bridges, a suspension bridge, wind turbines, railway tracks, and vehicles.

design.typography:
Two families only, a strict serif-for-headings / sans-for-everything-else pairing.
• Serif (display): the wordmark "Korkut Kaynardag, PhD" (≈15–16 px, medium weight, letterspaced ~0.02em), the H1 "About Me" (≈48–52 px, semibold/bold, tight tracking, #23201C), all H2s ("Biography", "At a glance — September 2026", "Career timeline" at ≈28–32 px, semibold), the timeline role titles (≈20–22 px, semibold) and the three big stat numbers (≈44–48 px). Letterforms show moderate-to-high stroke contrast, bracketed serifs, a flat-topped "A", a ball-ish terminal on the "a" and old-style-looking figures in "2026" — consistent with Playfair Display, Lora, Libre Baskerville or EB Garamond; Playfair Display is the closest single guess for the H1 given the thin hairlines at that size. [Exact family cannot be proven from a phone photo — best guess.]
• Sans (text/UI): all body paragraphs (≈17–18 px, line-height ≈1.7–1.75, #3D3A35), the "link coming soon" row (≈13–14 px), the stat labels (≈12–13 px), the timeline date ranges (≈12 px, uppercase, letterspaced ~0.08em, brick red), the timeline organisation line (≈15 px) and description line (≈14–15 px), and the CV button label (≈15 px). Double-storey "a", open apertures, fairly wide default tracking, geometric-leaning round "o" and "e" — consistent with Inter, DM Sans, Jost or Poppins. [Best guess only.]
• Hierarchy note: there is no bold text inside body paragraphs anywhere on the page; emphasis is carried entirely by the serif/sans switch, size and the red accent.

design.texture_and_effects: Backgrounds are flat warm ivory with no gradient, vignette or visible large-scale pattern. In the sharpest early frames (v01_001, v01_002) a very fine vertical striation runs across the upper ivory area, which would read as a faint paper/linen texture — but the same striation drifts and changes orientation between frames and merges into the heavy rainbow moire that dominates from v01_008 onward, so it is most likely camera/LCD moire and NOT a real CSS texture. Treat "faint vertical linen texture" as unproven; flat ivory (#F6F1E5) is the safe reproduction, optionally with a 2–3 % noise/grain overlay to match the paper feeling of the serif type. No drop shadows are visible on any element (the portrait and the CV button both sit flat on the ivory). The only rounded geometry is the photo (~12 px) and the CV button (~8 px). No hover states, transitions, parallax, scroll-reveal or any other motion can be observed: the only movement across the 36 frames is plain wheel scrolling, and the header stays perfectly pinned with no shrink, no shadow appearing and no colour change. The thin scrollbar on the right belongs to the IDE preview, not to a styled site scrollbar, and the rounded corners around the whole ivory area are the preview card's, not the website's.

misses.claim: "Single centred content column of roughly 1050–1150 px inside a ~1400 px-wide preview viewport (so ... roughly 130–150 px of ivory margin either side)"
misses.correction: Measured in v01_002: the content column's ink runs x=120 → x=1541 (H1, H2, body all start at exactly 120; the portrait/CV-button right edge is 1541 and the link-row divider dies at x≈1540). The preview card's interior is x≈77 → 1612. So the content occupies 92.5% of the viewport and the gutters are only ~47 frame px ≈ 40 CSS px per side, NOT 130–150. Cross-checking against type (body cap height 17 frame px → ~17 px font) gives scale ≈1.39 frame px/CSS px, i.e. content ≈1020 CSS px (max-w-5xl) inside a preview viewport of only ~1050–1175 CSS px — not 1400. Design consequence the first pass missed entirely: the client has only ever seen this page in a ~1100px-wide preview. On his real 1440–1920px monitor the same max-w-5xl cap will leave 200–450px of empty ivory per side, which will NOT look like what he approved.

misses.claim: H1 "About Me" ≈48–52 px; stat numbers ≈44–48 px; wordmark ≈15–16 px
misses.correction: All the display sizes are inflated by ~30%. Measured cap heights in v01_002: H1 "A" = 35 frame px, H2 "B" = 26, body "I" = 17, wordmark "K" = 17. Width check confirms it: "About Me" is 221 frame px wide = 4.3 em of a Playfair-like serif → H1 ≈ 36 CSS px (text-4xl), not 48–52. "Biography" 168 frame px → H2 ≈ 27 px. Wordmark 277 frame px for 21 chars → ≈18 px, i.e. the wordmark is the SAME optical size as the body copy, not smaller. In v01_019 (same-frame ratio, immune to camera scale) the stat figures are 34 frame px tall against an H2 cap of 23.5 → stat numbers ≈ 39 px. Real hierarchy fact: the H1 (36) and the stat numbers (39) are essentially the same size, so the page has no single dominant display size — it is a restrained, small-display design, not the dramatic 50px-headline page the first pass describes.

misses.claim: "Portrait figure: ... corner radius ≈10–12 px" and "CV button: ... ~8 px corner radius"
misses.correction: Both radii are far smaller — the page is essentially square-cornered. Edge-tracing the CV button's top-left in v01_002: its left edge is at x=1123 at y=884 and stays at 1123 at y=886, 888, 892, 898, 905 — zero measurable inset in the first rows below the top edge → radius ≤ 2 CSS px. The photo's left edge is 1128 at y=475 and 1125 from y=479 down (3 frame px of inset over 4 rows), and its top edge moves only 2 frame px over 10 columns → radius ≈ 3–5 CSS px. Camera blur can only EXAGGERATE a corner arc, never shrink it, so these are upper bounds. Rebuild with rounded-[4px] on the photo and a square (or rounded-sm) button; 10–12 px / 8 px would visibly soften a design whose whole character is hard-edged and print-like.

misses.claim: "Sticky top header bar ≈56–64 px tall"
misses.correction: The header is ~30–50% taller. In v01_002 the page is at scroll 0: the preview card's interior top is y=62 and the header's bottom hairline is at y=159–161 (row-dip of 9.9 against an empty ivory column) → header = 98 frame px ≈ 72–88 CSS px, i.e. roughly 5rem. Corroborated in v01_023, where content is hard-clipped at y≈140 with the card top at y≈46. Reproduce with h-20 / py-6, not h-14.

misses.claim: "Sticky site header: full-width ivory bar, serif wordmark left ... wordmark at the left content edge"
misses.correction: The wordmark is NOT on the content edge. In v01_002 the wordmark's ink starts at x=104 while the H1 "About Me", the H2 "Biography" and every body line all start at exactly x=120 — a consistent 16 frame px ≈ 12 CSS px offset (confirmed in v01_001 at 120 vs 133 and v01_003 at 103 vs 117). The header bar therefore uses a wider container (or smaller horizontal padding) than the article column. Either reproduce that offset deliberately or fix it — but don't assume they share a container.

misses.claim: "Social/profile link row: three inline items spread across the content width"
misses.correction: They are not spread — it is a left-aligned flex row with a fixed gap that stops well short of the right edge. Measured item left edges in v01_001: x≈154, 562, 908; item 1 ends ≈506 and item 2 starts 562 (gap 56), item 2 ends ≈848 and item 3 starts 908 (gap 60). So a constant ~56–60 frame px ≈ 45 CSS px gap, not space-between. The row's right end (≈1235) is over 300 frame px short of the content right edge (1541). Separately, the row's left edge (glyph ink x=137 in v01_002) sits ~17 frame px ≈ 12 CSS px to the RIGHT of the content edge (120) — so the link row is visibly out of alignment with the H1, the divider and the Biography text above and below it. Use `flex gap-12`, and note the indent is probably an accident worth correcting.

misses.claim: "Timeline entry (×5): hollow circle marker (≈8–9 px diameter ...) sitting on a 1 px vertical rail"
misses.correction: Two errors. (a) Size: in the 7× crop of v01_030 the ring's outer diameter is ≈19–20 frame px ≈ 13–14 CSS px with a ~2 px stroke — roughly 50% larger than stated. (b) The dot does not sit ON the rail: the rail starts ~5–7 frame px (≈4–5 CSS px) BELOW the bottom of the ring, with clear ivory between them (visible in v01_030, v01_036, v01_019). And the rail is SEGMENTED, not one continuous spine — in v01_036 it runs from under dot 1 (crop y≈305) only to the bottom of that entry's description (y≈590), then stops dead for ~118 crop px before dot 2 at y≈708; same pattern for every entry in v01_021, v01_024, v01_027. Rebuild as a `border-left` on each entry (dot rendered separately above it), NOT as one full-height line with dots on it.

misses.claim: Page background "≈ #F6F1E5 (the camera renders it warmer, around #F7EEDC; the true value is probably slightly cooler and lighter)"
misses.correction: Backwards — the camera is not adding the warmth, so do not cool it down. In v01_002 the same frame renders the IDE's white "Share" label as (204,203,205) and the near-black toolbar as (52,57,61), i.e. the capture's white balance is neutral-to-slightly-COOL. Against that neutral reference the page background measures (232,215,193): R−B = +39, or 17% of its own mean. #F6F1E5 has R−B = 7%; the first pass's own alternative #F7EEDC is 11%. The real background is therefore at least as warm as #F7EEDC and plausibly warmer (~#F5EAD6 / #F3E8D4) — a proper sand/parchment, not a near-white ivory. This is the single most visible colour decision on the page and the first pass advises moving it the wrong direction.

misses.claim: "Heading / wordmark ink — very dark warm near-black, ≈ #23201C"
misses.correction: The heading ink is neutral, not warm. Darkest-25-pixel means in v01_002: H1 "About Me" = #3D3C3B (R−B = +3), H2 "Biography" = #4E4948 (+5), wordmark = #5E5B58 (+6) — measured in the same frame where the background is +39 warm. So the headings are a neutral charcoal sitting on a warm ground; that cool/warm tension is a big part of why the page reads crisp rather than sepia. (The sans samples do come out warmer — body #4F4336 (+25), muted #7B7569 (+19) — but thin antialiased strokes pick up background bleed, so that warmth is not evidence of a different ink.) Use a neutral #2B2B2A-ish charcoal, not #23201C.

misses.claim: "CV button fill — desaturated slate blue-grey, ≈ #6E7F8C"
misses.correction: It is considerably bluer than that. Median fill in v01_002 is (136,144,159): B > G > R with B−R = +23, measured in a frame whose page background is R−B = +39. The relative swing across the page/button boundary is ~62 points on the R−B axis — a decisive cool steel/denim blue, not a near-grey. #6E7F8C is almost neutral and will under-sell the one cool accent on an otherwise entirely warm page.

misses.claim: The first pass never states whether the sticky header is opaque or translucent, only that it "never moves" and "does NOT gain a shadow".
misses.correction: Provable and worth pinning: the header is FULLY OPAQUE and hard-clips content. Row-mean test on v01_023, comparing x=150–460 (directly over the "Career timeline" heading) against x=700–1010 (empty ivory at the same rows): the difference is a flat 2.5–3.9 for every row from y=109 to y=139, then jumps to 12.0 / 22.9 / 30.3 at y=142/145/148 where the glyph bottoms emerge. Zero bleed-through above y=140 → no `backdrop-filter`, no rgba background. Same test shows no darkening gradient below the rule → no scroll shadow, confirming the first pass on that point. A faint bottom hairline persists while scrolled (row dip 1.5–1.6 at y=136–138 in the empty column).

misses.claim: "body paragraphs (≈17–18 px, line-height ≈1.7–1.75)"
misses.correction: Line-height is tighter. Measured line-band tops in v01_002: 553, 590, 630, 669 (para 1) and 732, 774, 812, 849 (para 2) → pitch 38.8 frame px against a body font of ≈23.4 frame px → line-height 1.62–1.66, i.e. Tailwind `leading-relaxed` (1.625). The paragraph gap is one extra ~24 frame px ≈ 17 CSS px, i.e. about 0.6 of a line, not a full blank line.

misses.claim: "text column ~60–63 % of content width ... media rail ~30 % ... gutter ~50–60 px"
misses.correction: Measured: text column 120 → ~1043 (930 frame px), gutter 1043 → 1127 (77 frame px ≈ 55 CSS px), media rail 1127 → 1541 (414 frame px). That is 65.4% / 5.4% / 29.1%. The text share is above the stated 60–63%, which matters because at 65% of a 1020px column the measure runs to ~670px — a long line for 17px type, and part of why the Biography block feels heavier than the timeline below it.

misses.claim: "Portrait figure: ... roughly 1.1–1.2:1 landscape, filling the media rail's full width."
misses.correction: Precise numbers: 414 × 381 frame px = 1.087:1 — near-square (≈298 × 274 CSS px), at the shallow end of the stated range. Its top edge (y=472) sits 9 px above the "Biography" cap top (481), i.e. the two columns share a row start. The gap from the photo's bottom to the CV button's top is 27 frame px ≈ 20 CSS px (photo bottom ≈854, button top 881), and the button matches the photo's width exactly (1123→1538 vs 1127→1541).

misses.claim: "State D ... the scrollbar thumb sits near (but not quite at) the bottom of its track" and "No footer is visible ... after the last timeline entry there is only empty ivory"
misses.correction: The conclusion is right but the first pass treats it as un-provable when it is provable. Cropping the preview scrollbar out of v01_033 and v01_035 shows the thumb reaching the bottom of the track (only the track's own ~12 frame px of bottom padding below it). So the page really does end there: there is definitively NO footer, no contact block, no copyright line. The thumb is ~30% of the track, so the whole /about page is about 3.3 viewports tall.

additions: Vertical rhythm, measured in v01_002 (frame px, and ÷1.39 for CSS): header rule (160) → H1 cap top (238) = 78 ≈ 56 px; H1 baseline (272) → link-row cap top (330) = 58 ≈ 42 px; link-row bottom (345) → divider (410) = 65 ≈ 47 px; divider (410) → "Biography" cap top (481) = 71 ≈ 51 px; H2 baseline (506) → first body line (552) = 46 ≈ 33 px. The first pass's "~56–72 px between major sections, ~24 px from an H2 to its first line" understates the H2→body gap by about half.

The divider under the link row spans the FULL content width, not just the text column: local-contrast values along y=410 in v01_002 run 6–9 from x≈170 continuously out to x=1530 and die to −0.5 at x=1545 — i.e. it terminates exactly at the media rail's right edge (1541). It is a section rule under both columns.

The "At a glance" band's bounding rules are at y≈293 and y≈472 in v01_019 → band height 179 frame px ≈ 129 CSS px, and the top rule sits only ~18 frame px ≈ 13 CSS px below the heading's baseline — a notably tight heading-to-rule gap that is easy to get wrong in a rebuild.

Timeline geometry (v01_030, 7× crop): dot centre x ≈157, rail x ≈158 (so the rail IS centred on the dot, ±2 px), entry text left edge x ≈193 → the text is indented ~36 frame px ≈ 26 CSS px from the dot centre. The rail continues ~17 frame px below the last description baseline before stopping.

The rail and the dot are two different colours, not one element: in the v01_030 crop the ring is a saturated red-brown while the rail is a pale warm hairline several steps lighter. Rebuild them as separate tokens (accent ring + border colour rail), not `border-current`.

Hamburger geometry (v01_002): bars occupy rows 97–101, 106–110, 115–119 and columns 1521–1552 → icon ≈32 × 23 frame px ≈ 23 × 17 CSS px, bars ~2.5 px, gaps ~4 px. It is wider than it is tall — dropping in a square 24×24 Lucide `menu` will not match. Its right edge sits ~44 CSS px inside the card edge, i.e. it clears the preview scrollbar rather than aligning to the content edge (1541).
The social-link glyph (v01_001, 8× crop) is a HORIZONTAL two-link chain — Lucide `link-2` shape — not the 45°-diagonal `link` glyph. Its ink height is 13 frame px ≈ 9–10 CSS px.

I tested whether each link item has an internal weight split (bold platform name + muted "— link coming soon"): it does NOT. Darkest-pixel contrast in v01_002 is 101 for "Google Scholar" vs 117 for "— link coming soon", and 123 vs 137 for the LinkedIn item — the trailing text is if anything marginally darker. The whole item is one uniform muted run, as the first pass said. Worth recording because the blurred frames read as though the name is bolder.

The CV button shows a faintly darker 1 px top and left edge against its own fill in the 9× crop of v01_002 — possibly a 1 px border a shade darker than the fill, possibly LCD edge ringing. Low confidence, but if a border is added it should be barely darker than the fill, never lighter.

No hover, focus or active state is observable anywhere in the 36 frames. The mouse cursor is a plain I-beam parked over empty ivory in v01_001–v01_006 and v01_015–v01_035 and never crosses a link, the CV button or the hamburger — so no interaction styling from this clip is approved, and any hover treatment in a rebuild is a new proposal.

Scale-free ratios for a rebuild that does not depend on guessing the CSS viewport (all from v01_002, as fractions of the 1421-frame-px content width): header height 6.9%; text column 65.4%; column gutter 5.4%; media rail 29.1%; body line pitch 2.73%; paragraph gap 1.7%; H1 ascender 2.60%; photo width 29.1% at 1.087:1.
critics.confidence_in_first_pass: Content, page structure, component inventory and the palette's ROLES are reliable — I found nothing wrong in the transcribed copy, the section order, the four scroll states, the sticky-header behaviour, the absence of a left sidebar, the absence of cards/shadows/badges, or the claim that red is used only on stat numbers, timeline dates and dots. Treat all of that as trustworthy. Do NOT trust any absolute number in the first pass: every measured quantity I re-checked was off — display type sizes inflated ~30% (H1 48–52 → 36), corner radii inflated 2–4× (10–12/8 → ~4/~0–2), header height understated (56–64 → ~80), the viewport and gutters wrong by a large margin (1400px/130–150px gutters → ~1100px/~40px gutters), and line-height overstated (1.7–1.75 → 1.625). Two alignment facts are also wrong in a way that changes the build (the wordmark does not share the content column's left edge; the link row is neither spread nor aligned to it). The one colour judgement to reverse outright is the background: the camera's white balance is neutral, so the warm cast is real and the true ivory is at least as warm as #F7EEDC, not cooler than #F6F1E5."

misses.claim: urls_and_filenames lists only ONE truncated left-panel text line, "…com..", tracked across frames as "m.. → om.. → com.. → .com.."
misses.correction: There are TWO stacked lines there, not one. Upscaled/auto-contrasted crops show an upper line whose visible tail is "on" and, directly beneath it, a second line whose visible tail is "<char>.com.." (one glyph is partly visible before the dot). The first pass merged the two into a single fragment and therefore dropped the "on" line entirely. Combined with the separate "…tom-doma/tom-domai" line lower down (= "custom-domain"), the panel holds at least three distinct truncated strings, which matters if the original Lovable project/domain step has to be reconstructed.

misses.claim: placeholders_and_gaps: "Turkish diacritics are inconsistent: the wordmark reads 'Korkut Kaynardag, PhD' (no ğ) and the body says 'Izmir Institute of Technology' (no İ), while 'Boğaziçi University' is correctly accented in both the Biography and the timeline."
misses.correction: The inconsistency list is incomplete: the same timeline line reads "Boğaziçi University, Istanbul, Turkey" — "Istanbul" is written with a plain Latin I, not "İstanbul", even though ğ and ç in "Boğaziçi" on that exact same line ARE correct. So the page mixes correct and incorrect Turkish diacritics inside one string. Carry it verbatim ("Boğaziçi University, Istanbul, Turkey") or fix all three consistently — do not silently normalise just one.

misses.claim: The first pass transcribed the text correctly but recorded no rule about it.
misses.correction: "Nondestructive" is spelled two different ways on the same page and both must survive a rebuild verbatim: UNHYPHENATED in the Biography paragraph 3 ("nondestructive damage detection") and in timeline entry 1 ("Research on structural health monitoring, nondestructive damage detection, smart sensors and smart cities."), but HYPHENATED in timeline entry 4 ("…and non-destructive testing systems.") and entry 5 ("Structural health monitoring and non-destructive testing systems."). A rebuild that normalises to one spelling loses a fact about the approved draft.

misses.claim: Both were transcribed but no dash convention was stated.
misses.correction: Two different dash conventions are in use for year ranges and must be reproduced exactly: the Biography uses an UNSPACED EN DASH inside parentheses — "(2023–2024)", "(2024–2026)"; the Career timeline uses a SPACED EM DASH — "2026 — PRESENT", "2024 — 2026", "2023 — 2024", "2016 — 2023", "2013 — 2016". Every other dash on the page is a spaced em dash ("Google Scholar — link coming soon", "At a glance — September 2026", "Patents — 1 granted, 1 pending", "Placeholder — the CV file will be attached here.").

misses.frame: v01_001 (wordmark) vs v01_009 (bio) and v01_024, v01_029 (timeline entry 4)
misses.claim: Not flagged.
misses.correction: "PhD" vs "Ph.D." is inconsistent and both spellings must be kept: the sticky wordmark is "Korkut Kaynardag, PhD" (no periods), while the Biography says "my Ph.D. from the Department of Civil Engineering" and the timeline role title is "Ph.D. & Graduate Research Assistant" (with periods, and an ampersand, not "and").

misses.claim: placeholders_and_gaps: "No footer is visible at the bottom of the page — after the last timeline entry there is only empty ivory; no contact block, copyright line or footer nav appears at the deepest scroll position (v01_033–v01_035)."
misses.correction: Overstated. At the deepest scroll position the preview scrollbar thumb still stops clearly short of the bottom of its track (a gap roughly half the thumb's own height), so the bottom of the /about page is never actually reached in this clip. What is provable is only: "no footer was seen in the scroll range captured". Whether a footer exists below is UNKNOWN, not absent. The visible ivory gap under the M.Sc. entry (~100 px) is consistent with ordinary section padding.

misses.claim: components: "Social/profile link row: three inline items spread across the content width"; layout repeats "spread across the content width".
misses.correction: They are NOT spread across the full content width. Measured on the zoomed crop, the row is left-clustered: "Google Scholar" starts at the content's left edge, and "ResearchGate — link coming soon" ends at only ~75 % of the content width, leaving the right quarter empty. The gap between items is roughly constant (~50–60 px), i.e. a flex row with a fixed gap, not `justify-content: space-between`. The hairline divider BELOW the row does span the full content width, which is what makes the row look short next to it.

misses.claim: layout_notes: "State D — frames v01_023 to v01_035 … Final move — frame v01_036: the user scrolls back UP".
misses.correction: The scroll-back-up starts one frame earlier, at v01_035, where the role title "Senior AI Engineer" becomes fully legible again after being cut off at the top edge in v01_033–v01_034; v01_036 continues that upward move until the "Career timeline" H2 is back in view. Also, v01_023–v01_034 is not one stable state: it contains at least three further downward steps (v01_023–024 with "Career timeline" clipped at top; v01_025–026 one entry lower; v01_027–034 deepest). Scrolling in this clip is near-continuous, not four discrete stops.

misses.claim: urls_and_filenames: "Left-panel dismissible chip, text cut off (partial): 'abl' / 'able' / 'ble' followed by an '×' close button"
misses.correction: Detail correction: the chip is a LIGHT / near-white filled rounded pill carrying DARK text (not a dark chip), and the "×" is OUTSIDE the pill, to its right, on the panel background. Only the tail "…able" is ever legible (clearest in v01_023). Still builder chrome, not site content — but the light fill is the strongest hint that it is a Lovable-branded badge rather than a warning banner.

additions: EVERY site string the first pass transcribed is confirmed character-for-character against high-zoom crops. Verified verbatim: the three link items "Google Scholar — link coming soon" / "LinkedIn — link coming soon" / "ResearchGate — link coming soon" (v01_001, v01_003); the button label "Download CV (coming soon)" and the two-line caption "Placeholder — the CV file will be attached here." (v01_009, v01_010); the three stat labels "Published articles", "Patents — 1 granted, 1 pending", "Awards from academic & industry-academia grants" (v01_014, v01_018); all four Biography paragraphs (v01_009, v01_011); all five timeline entries with dates, titles, org lines and descriptions (v01_029, v01_036). No sentence, heading, list item or caption was dropped by the first pass.

The third stat label breaks mid-hyphen — "Awards from academic & industry-" / "academia grants" (v01_014, v01_018, v01_019). The source string therefore contains a real hyphen in "industry-academia" and an ampersand "&", not the word "and". The wrap is a consequence of the narrow third cell, not of a second sentence.

Timeline entry 1's description has NO Oxford comma — "…smart sensors and smart cities." (v01_020, v01_036) — whereas the Biography's version of the same list DOES — "…smart sensors, and smart cities." (v01_009, v01_011). Another verbatim-preservation trap.

The site's only identity string anywhere in this clip is "Korkut Kaynardag, PhD". The words "Waves and Data", "wavesanddata" or "wavesanddata.com" never appear on the rendered page in any of the 36 frames — the domain only ever shows up (truncated) inside the builder's left panel. If the rebuild is supposed to be branded "Waves and Data", that branding does not yet exist in the approved draft.

The link row has exactly THREE items and no more — no Email, ORCID, GitHub, X/Twitter or phone entry is present (v01_001–v01_007). All three are plain muted text with a chain-link glyph; none is an anchor.

In the builder toolbar the path field renders as a grey "/" followed by "about" in bold white (v01_001 zoomed) — i.e. the stored route value is "about" and the slash is chrome. Project pill confirmed as "Korkut's Research Hub" with a globe icon. Toolbar actions confirmed left-to-right: Share (dark) · Upgrade (violet, lightning bolt) · Publish (blue).

Windows clock confirmed: "10:08 AM 9/15/2026" from v01_004 onward, rolling to "10:09 AM" in v01_011 and back to "10:08 AM" rendering in later frames (camera/JPEG noise on the minute digit); input language "ENG". The 2026 dating of the content is therefore genuine machine time, not a typo — do not "correct" any year.

Header structure confirmed with no hidden element: sticky bar (serif wordmark left, 3-bar hamburger right) → full-width 1 px hairline → H1 "About Me" → link row → second full-width 1 px hairline → H2 "Biography". There is no kicker, eyebrow, tagline, breadcrumb or subtitle anywhere between them (v01_002 zoomed).

In every timeline entry the organisation/location line is set in the DARK body ink while the description line below it is MUTED grey — a two-level contrast step inside one entry (clearest in v01_029, v01_036). The vertical rail also reads as a short segment per entry, starting at each hollow circle and stopping before the next one, rather than one unbroken line down the whole section.

Frame v01_008 is a double-exposed / rolling-shutter smear of the Biography block and carries no unique text; frame v01_012 is similarly unreadable. Nothing is lost by ignoring both — every line they contain is legible in v01_007 and v01_009–v01_011.
critics.confidence_in_first_pass: High on transcription, moderate on framing. Every word of site copy the first pass reported is confirmed exactly against high-zoom crops — no mistranscribed words, no dropped sentences, no missed headings, list items, captions or placeholder markers, and the section ordering is right. What it missed is flagging-level rather than reading-level: three in-page consistency traps (nondestructive/non-destructive, PhD/Ph.D., en-dash vs em-dash year ranges), one further diacritics case ("Istanbul"), one whole truncated line in the builder's left panel, plus two overstated claims (the link row is left-clustered rather than full-width, and the bottom of the page was never actually reached so "no footer" is unproven rather than established).

first.what_it_is: A phone-camera recording of a ViewSonic monitor showing the Lovable (lovable.dev) AI app builder, with the preview pane open on a draft personal academic site titled "Korkut's Research Hub" / page "Homepage". Across the 10 seconds the person does nothing but scroll the preview slowly from the top of the homepage down past three content blocks: the hero (eyebrow + H1 + two bio paragraphs + headshot + two buttons), the "Why the educational sections exist" essay with a 4-item numbered list, and the "Explore the topics" three-card grid. The camera drifts and refocuses; no clicks, no edits, no menu opens. The left third of the screen is the Lovable chat panel, mostly cropped by the monitor edge, where the last user message reads "ok before going forward, can you publish this free on 🔗 wavesanddata.com…" — i.e. the draft in these frames is the design he has approved and now wants published on his own domain. Note: in this preview width the site's navigation is collapsed to a hamburger at the top right; no left sidebar menu is visible anywhere in this clip.

Proof, character by character: the address bar in v02_003–v02_006 reads `https://lovable.dev/chats/9994de28-52ce-4af7-8d44-37ec65de63bb?artifact=project%3A34000a66-3304-4430-a914-5c4a1656cce7` — the `/chats/<uuid>?artifact=project%3A<uuid>` route is Lovable's. Corroborating Lovable chrome: dark near-black left chat rail with a project breadcrumb, a pill-shaped project chip at the top of the preview toolbar with a small globe/shield glyph reading "Korkut's Research Hub", a row of preview-mode icons (page/file, `</>` code view, database/Supabase-style stack icon, then a monitor/responsive icon and a circular refresh arrow), a centred page selector "Homepage" with a `⌄` chevron and an "open in new tab" ↗ box icon, then "Share", a purple gradient "⚡ Upgrade" pill and a blue "Publish" pill at the far right — that Share / Upgrade / Publish triad plus "Plan custom-doma[in]" in the chat rail is Lovable's, not Wix's editor and not Claude's artifact viewer. screens.body_text:
Korkut Kaynardag, PhD

ACADEMIC & RESEARCH PORTFOLIO

Korkut Kaynardag, PhD

This webpage introduces you to three things: myself, my research, and the topics I use in my research — on the mechanics and physics side, wave propagation and dynamics; on the data side, AI, signal processing, system identification, optimization and estimation.

I am an Assistant Professor in the Department of Civil Engineering at Izmir Institute of Technology, specializing in structural health monitoring (SHM), non-destructive testing (NDT) and sound target analysis — deployed offline through developed software and tools, via cloud data processing, or on-board via microchips.

About me →

My research areas

[Bold runs inside paragraph 1, exactly as rendered: "myself", "my research", "the topics I use in my research". The em dashes are true em dashes with spaces around them. "About me →" is a filled blue button; "My research areas" is a plain text/ghost button to its right.]

screens.body_text:
Why the educational sections exist

As a civil engineer, I met vibrations, waves, signals, system identification, estimation, optimization and machine learning only after my undergraduate degree. Learning them was challenging — it took a long time and many repetitions to really understand:

1. when these topics, methods and algorithms are used,

2. what they actually solve,

3. for what problems they are used (similar ideas come up more than once in different topics and applications), and

4. how deeply they are connected with each other — which was my Aha! moment.

Had I started learning with the answers to those four questions — plus knowing which books and resources to use — I believe I would have learned faster and more efficiently. So I created these sections for new researchers, students and anyone interested, where I attempt to answer the four questions and share the books I found most useful. My goal: faster, more efficient learning, better comprehension, and more time left for research — or simply for learning more.

["Aha!" in item 4 is set in italics, including the exclamation mark; "moment." that follows is roman. The list is a real ordered list: numerals "1." … "4." hang to the left of the text block, wrapped lines in item 3 indent to align under "for", not under the numeral.]

design.typography:
Two families, cleanly split by role.

SERIF (logotype, h1, h2, card h3): a transitional / old-style serif with noticeable thick-thin contrast, bracketed serifs, fairly small x-height relative to the caps, a double-storey 'g' with an open lower loop, and a slightly flared 'y' tail. h1 "Korkut Kaynardag, PhD" is ~46–50px, weight ~600 (semibold, not black), letter-spacing near 0 or very slightly negative, line-height ~1.15. h2 ("Why the educational sections exist", "Explore the topics") ~30–33px, same weight and colour. Card h3 ~21–23px, same family, line-height ~1.3. The sticky logotype is the same serif at ~16–17px with slightly loose tracking (~0.01em). Family candidates, in order of likeness: Source Serif 4 / Source Serif Pro, Spectral, Libre Baskerville, Lora. It is NOT a high-contrast display face like Playfair and NOT a slab.

SANS (everything else — body, eyebrow, buttons, card body, "Read more"): a neutral grotesque with a double-storey 'a', single-storey 'g', straight-cut terminals and fairly open apertures — reads as Inter (or system-ui / Helvetica-class fallback). Body ~17–18px, weight 400, line-height ~1.7–1.75 (measured: lines sit ~30px apart at 17px), colour #3C4351. Bold runs inside paragraph 1 are weight 600–700 in the same family and the same colour (no colour change). Eyebrow is ~12px, weight 500–600, ALL CAPS, letter-spacing ~0.12–0.14em, muted #8B8175. Button labels ~15px weight 600 ("About me") and ~15–16px weight 400–500 ("My research areas"). Card body ~15px, line-height ~1.6. "Read more →" ~14px, weight 500. Numbered-list items are body-size sans at 17px.

Italics appear once, on "Aha!" in list item 4 — same sans, italic.

I wrote them for newcomers who want the big picture: how these topics connect, and how to approach learning them, without diving into the equations and formalism of a textbook or lecture. They reflect my own path into this field — but everyone's path is different, so I'd encourage you to read a few other guides alongside these rather than relying on just one.

Research areas

Structural Health Monitoring & Non-Destructive Testing
The science of monitoring and testing structures to detect and characterize defects before they become failures — applied to tall buildings, masonry buildings and bridges, suspension bridges, wind turbines and railway tracks.

Vibration Analysis & Acoustic Wave Propagation
The mechanics and physics foundation of SHM and NDT: how waves travel through structures, and what they reveal about hidden damage.

misses.claim: "Text starts ~80px in from the content-card's left edge and the measure runs to roughly 55–60% of the preview width, leaving a very large empty right gutter (~40% of the viewport) on every line" / "the measure is around 700–760px".
misses.correction: WRONG, and self-contradictory (90–95 chars cannot fit in 700–760px at 17–18px). Measured in v04_001: preview pane's left edge x=44, body text left edge x=81, longest prose line right edge x=1424 (the 'big picture' placeholder L1). Ivory runs unbroken to the frame's right edge x=1663 in EVERY frame, so the viewport is at least 1620px wide in frame units. The prose measure is therefore >=83% of the visible viewport with a right gutter of at most ~15%, not 40%. Left padding is tiny (~37px of frame ≈ 22–24 CSS px), so the design is a near-full-width container with a max-width cap on paragraphs only. Rebuilding this as a 55–60% column would be badly wrong.

misses.correction: INVERTED. The bracketed italic placeholders are DARKER than the lead paragraph, not lighter. Local-background-normalised ink (p0.5 of value/local-bg, lower = darker): lead paragraph 0.48 (f001), 0.52 (f002), 0.53 (f003); 'big picture' placeholder 0.37/0.39/0.36/0.37 in f001/f003/f004/f005 and 'how to learn' placeholder 0.36/0.39/0.37 in f004/f006/f009. The lead/intro paragraph is the page's MUTED text (a 'text-muted-foreground'/opacity treatment); the placeholders are normal body ink set in italic.

misses.correction: WRONG on both counts. Identical size: lead L1 is 93 characters across 1305px = 14.03 px/char; placeholder L1 is 95 characters across 1342px = 14.13 px/char — a 0.7% difference. (3) INK: it does NOT measure as the near-black heading ink. p0.5 = 0.46 (f001) against H1 0.24 and H2 0.34 — it sits in the same tonal band as the muted lead paragraph (0.48), so it is a secondary/muted grey, not the primary heading ink.

misses.correction: IMPRECISE — the right end of both rules is off-camera. misses.claim: "H1 'Vibrations and Waves' is roughly 46–50px"; "H2s… roughly 28–32px"; body "~17–18px with generous line-height around 1.7–1.75".
misses.correction: ~15% HIGH on the headings, slightly high on line-height. Measured v04_001: H1 cap 'V' = 43px, H1 x-height = 29px, H2 cap 'T' = 29px, body cap 'T' = 19–20px, body line pitch = 45.5px (line tops 363 / 409 / 454). Two independent methods (cap-height ÷ cap-per-em, and mean character advance) put H1 at 2.2–2.5× body and H2 at 1.45–1.50× body, with H1/H2 = 1.5. At a 17–18px body that is H1 ≈ 38–44px and H2 ≈ 25–27px. Line-height = 45.5 ÷ body em (≈27.5 by advance) ≈ 1.60–1.65, not 1.70–1.75. Express these as ratios in the rebuild (H1 2.3em, H2 1.5em, leading 1.6) rather than the first pass's absolutes.

misses.claim: "DOCUMENT CARD — sans throughout: title ~16px semibold dark; the two meta lines ~13–14px regular in the light gray" (i.e. the title smaller than the 17–18px body, and the two sub-lines one tier).

misses.claim: Listed under components as a page rule but described as "Used twice at the top of the page: once under the byline, once between the lead paragraph and the first H2" — leaving it ambiguous whether the first rule belongs to the fixed byline.

additions: MEASURED TONAL LADDER (p0.5 of pixel value ÷ local background; lower = darker ink). H1 0.24 · H2 0.24–0.35 · doc-card title 0.31 · bracketed italic placeholders 0.36–0.39 · byline 0.46 · lead paragraph 0.48–0.53 · doc description 0.54 · doc meta line 0.62–0.64 · 'Download' label and icon 0.63–0.68 (the single lightest element on the page). Six distinct tones, not the first pass's four — and the ordering of the middle band is the reverse of what it reported.

SERIF IDENTIFICATION NARROWED (supports, and tightens, the first pass's guess). v04_001 H1: cap height 43px (y=276→319), x-height 29px (y=289→318) → x-height/cap ≈ 0.67, and lower still (~0.66) once the ~1.5px blur spread is removed. That is an OLD-STYLE ratio: EB Garamond 0.666, Crimson Pro 0.652, Times 0.677. It positively RULES OUT the other candidates the first pass hedged with — Lora 0.739, Libre Baskerville 0.754, Merriweather 0.774, Noto Serif 0.75, Playfair Display 0.739 would all show a visibly bigger x-height. Pick from the Garamond/Crimson/Times class.

THE MEASURE IS TOO LONG — a real design defect to fix, not just a spec to copy. Lines run 89–95 characters: v04_001 lead L1 = 93 chars, v04_001 placeholder L1 = 95 chars, v04_006 placeholder L1 = 89 chars. That is far past the 60–75ch comfortable range for an academic text page. Combined with the corrected geometry (measure ≥83% of viewport), the page is currently a very wide, lightly-padded column — worth capping at ~70ch in the rebuild and telling him why.

THE PREVIEW IS NOT A DESKTOP WIDTH. Reconciling a 93-character line at 17–18px (≈760–800 CSS px of text) against a measured 1343px of frame implies a camera scale of ~1.6–1.7, which puts the rendered viewport at roughly 950–1000 CSS px — a small-laptop/tablet width, not a 1440px desktop. This is almost certainly WHY the left menu is collapsed to a hamburger: the clip may be showing the site BELOW its desktop breakpoint. The layout Dr. Kaynardag actually asked for ('sol kisimda menu olcak hep') may well exist and simply not be rendered at this width. Do not conclude from v04 that the desktop left rail is missing.

ICONOGRAPHY, read at 4–5× zoom (v04_009, crop x=60–400 y=650–790 and x=1180–1420 y=660–720). File glyph: a rounded-rectangle document outline with a notched/folded top-right corner and 2–3 short horizontal rules inside, thin uniform stroke, centred in the tile. Its ink measures 0.49–0.51 — a mid grey, the same tone as the muted lead paragraph, noticeably lighter than the doc title beside it. Download glyph: a downward arrow sitting on a shallow tray/baseline, ~24px wide in frame units, with a ~15px gap to the word 'Download'; icon and label measure identically (0.63 vs 0.64), so they are one coloured unit.

VERTICAL RHYTHM, expressed scale-free so it survives the unknown camera scale (v04_005, where four section boundaries are in one frame). Body line pitch P ≈ 45–50px. H2 top → its first body line top = 69–77px ≈ 1.5P. Last body line top → next H2 top = 130–133px ≈ 2.8P. So the space above a heading is about 3× the space below it — a tight heading-to-text bond inside generous section breaks. (This matches the first pass's 70px/24–28px figures; noting it because it is the one spacing claim that survives measurement.)

ZERO ACCENT COLOUR — now with quantitative backing rather than an eyeball call. Taking the 200 darkest pixels of each text run and reading their mean RGB: H1 (31,40,36), lead (74,75,57), placeholder (54,49,41), byline (78,82,76), doc title (52,41,36), doc meta (95,96,85), Download (117,109,95), file glyph (81,83,73) — against a page reference of (149,144,130). Every run's hue tracks the page's own warm cast (R−B between +2 and +22, matching the background's +19); not one shows the blue, violet or red excursion a link or accent colour would produce. The ivory + graphite + grey reading is confirmed, not merely assumed.

THE PAGE CANVAS IS WARMER THAN THE FIRST PASS'S #F4F0E7. Large flat samples: v04_009 below the card (168,163,152), v04_009 far right (164,157,144), v04_001 right gutter (183,175,159), v04_006 mid-page (173,169,155). Channel ratios cluster at R:G:B ≈ 1.00 : 0.96 : 0.89, whereas #F4F0E7 is 1.00 : 0.98 : 0.95. Since a uniform exposure change preserves sRGB channel ratios, the true canvas is more saturated than #F4F0E7 — closer to #F7F2E6 / #F6F1E5. Caveat: the camera's shadows read blue (the editor chrome samples at (47,64,71) where the true value is near-neutral), so there is a colour-temperature split in the capture; treat this as 'warmer than stated' rather than an exact hex.

FLATNESS CONFIRMED, WITH THE LIMIT STATED. Band means across x=60–1400 stepping y=600→820 in v04_009 vary only 160–172 in R with no monotonic trend, and the variation correlates with the moire fringe spacing rather than with height. There is no card fill, no border and no shadow behind the document row, and no section banding. The ~19-point R difference between the frame's centre and its far right is lens vignetting (it appears in frames with no content there), not a page gradient.

SCROLL IS PLAIN AND UNANIMATED — verifiable, not just assumed. Content displacement between v04_001 and v04_003 is 211–215px measured two independent ways (rule 2 at y=546→332; lead L1 top at y=363→148), and every glyph keeps identical ink density at every scroll position (the same placeholder paragraph measures 0.36–0.39 at y≈700, 490, 290 and 100). If there were a fade-in-on-scroll or an opacity reveal, that number would change with position. It does not. No parallax, no sticky section headers, no entrance animation.

NON-DESIGN ARTEFACT worth naming so it is not rebuilt: a single dark speck sits at x≈400, y≈90–96 in v04_007, v04_008 and v04_009, in the page area between the byline and the first paragraph. It is stationary across three frames in which both the camera and the page content are static, and at 6× zoom it is an isolated 2×3px blob with no letterform. It is a dead pixel or dust on the monitor, not a bullet, marker or glyph.

MINOR, for the record: the route field reads '/vibrations+waves' in v04_001 and unambiguously '/vibrations-waves' in v04_002. The hyphen reading is correct; the plus is a motion-blur artefact of the first frame. The first pass's kebab-case conclusion stands.
critics.confidence_in_first_pass: Moderate. The transcription, the page structure, the scroll stitching, the builder identification (Lovable / "Korkut's Research Hub" / /vibrations-waves), the serif-heading + sans-body split, the fixed byline and hamburger, the absence of accent colour, the absence of figures, and the placeholder inventory all hold up under pixel measurement. What does not hold up is nearly every quantitative design value: the column geometry is wrong by a wide margin (81–85% measure, not 55–60%), the text tone hierarchy is inverted (the lead paragraph is the page's muted text, the bracketed placeholders are darker), the byline's size and weight are wrong, heading sizes are ~15% high, the document row's geometry and alignment are wrong in three respects, and two claims — the divider under the card and the absence of a footer — assert things the frames do not show. Treat the first pass as a reliable content and structure inventory, and re-derive every number, colour role and alignment from the measurements above before building.

misses.claim: "Korkut Kaynardag, PhD" is position:fixed ... this is not a sticky header bar (there is no bar, no background, no border, no blur); they are two bare fixed text/icon elements floating directly on the page canvas" and "body text scrolls underneath it on the transparent ivory ... which is arguably a bug to fix in the rebuild"

Proof: in v04_006 the H2 "How to learn this topic" sits at y=153-184. v04_007 is scrolled only ~85px further — verified independently on every other line ("Recommended books & resources" 405->320, its placeholder 485->399 and 528->445, "Documents" 662->583, card title 762->678, meta 800->717, desc 839->753). screens.body_text:
Korkut Kaynardag, PhD

My Research Areas

My research focuses on Structural Health Monitoring (SHM) and Non-Destructive Testing (NDT): the science of monitoring and testing structures to detect and characterize defects before they become failures.

Overview

Because these fields rely heavily on vibration analysis, acoustic wave propagation, data analytics, and machine learning, my path also took me through industry, where I worked as a Senior AI Engineer on sound source tracking. The documents below introduce these topics, and I've also included a presentation that walks through my master's and PhD work in more depth.

You'll also find these documents under the Gallery section. I wrote them for newcomers who want the big picture: how these topics connect, and how to approach learning them, without diving into the equations and formalism of a textbook or lecture. They reflect my own path into this field — but everyone's path is different, so I'd encourage you to read a few other guides alongside these rather than relying on just one.

Research areas

Structural Health Monitoring & Non-Destructive Testing
The science of monitoring and testing structures to detect and characterize defects before they become failures — applied to tall buildings, masonry buildings and bridges, suspension bridges, wind turbines and railway tracks.

Vibration Analysis & Acoustic Wave Propagation
The mechanics and physics foundation of SHM and NDT: how waves travel through structures, and what they reveal about hidden damage.

Sound Source Tracking
Acoustic wave-based monitoring developed in industry — sound target analysis for vehicle monitoring, deployed on-board via microchips.

Data Analytics & Machine Learning
Signal processing, system identification, estimation, optimization and AI — deployed offline through software and tools, or through cloud data processing.

critics.confidence_in_first_pass: Moderate. Content, IA, voice and the broad design DNA (flat warm ivory, serif headings over humanist sans, hairlines as the only structure, no cards/shadows/accent colour, no imagery) are correct and well observed. But several load-bearing structural specifics are wrong or invented: the grid's vertical and horizontal dividers do not exist, the header has no secondary tint, the content column is flush-left with a ~220px empty right margin rather than centred, the measure is ~95-100 characters rather than ~75, the body is ~19-20px rather than 17-18, the wordmark is ~21px bold rather than 16px, there are two body sizes rather than one, and the repeating rows/cells carry 24-35px of internal indent that was not noticed. A rebuild following pass 1 literally would come out narrower, centred, over-ruled and lighter-typed than the draft the professor approved.

critics.confidence_in_first_pass: High on site content, lower on app chrome. Every sentence of site copy the first pass transcribed — the lede, both Overview paragraphs, all four card bodies, all four download-row titles and subtitles, and the truncated \"Also on this site\" paragraph — matches the frames word for word at 2-5x magnification; no heading, list item, nav label, \"coming soon\" marker or section ordering is missing or wrong, and its \"no figures, no images, no accent colour\" finding holds across all 14 frames. Its real weaknesses are outside the site: one flatly wrong toolbar label (\"Attached files\" → \"Uploaded files\"), a UUID segment presented as high-confidence that is genuinely ambiguous, an artifact-id group marked illegible that is in fact readable in two steady frames, an impossible 4-minute timestamp range for a 7.2 s clip, and several content relationships (lede/card-1 duplication, three degree spellings, the user's own underlined wavesanddata.com link, confirmed sticky header, ~20-25% of the page still unfilmed) that it observed in pieces but never connected.

first.what_it_is: A 7.5-second phone recording of a ViewSonic monitor showing one page of Korkut Kaynardag's draft academic site — the **Contact** page — open inside a Claude Artifact preview on claude.ai, running in Microsoft Edge (dark theme). Frames 001–008 hold still on the top of the page (sticky wordmark header, H1 "Contact", the lead paragraph, and the start of "Where to find me"). Around frame 009 the page is scrolled down roughly 300 px in one flick — frame 009 catches it mid-motion with double-image ghosting — and frames 010–015 settle on the lower state, where "Where to find me" is complete (Department / Email / Office) and the "Elsewhere" section with three greyed-out profile links comes into view. The sticky top bar (wordmark left, hamburger button right) does not move during the scroll. The mouse pointer drifts around x≈745 in the empty right half of the content column; nothing is clicked, no menu is opened, no text is typed. The whole clip is a slow read-through of one finished page, not an edit.
first.app_or_tool: **Claude Artifacts on claude.ai, viewed in Microsoft Edge (dark theme), Windows.** Evidence: (1) the URL query string `?artifact=project%3A34000a66-3304-4430-a914-5c4a1656cce7` — the `artifact=` parameter with a URL-encoded `project:` prefix is claude.ai's artifact-viewer form, not Wix/Lovable/v0; (2) the browser tab title reads "Build webpage with provided files" with a small orange/red Claude favicon — a Claude conversation title, not a project name; (3) the artifact toolbar across the top of the preview: a globe-icon pill naming the artifact **"Korkut's Research Hub"**, then a document icon, a `</>` code icon and a layers/stack icon (preview / code / versions), then a monitor/viewport icon, a circular-arrow reload icon, the current route `/ contact` with a chevron dropdown (route picker for a multi-page artifact), an external-open icon, and at the right **Share**, a purple lightning **Upgrade** pill and a blue **Publish** pill — this is Claude's artifact chrome; Wix has a left Editor panel and a "Publish" at top-right but no `</>` / route-picker of this shape, Lovable and v0 show their own logos and a chat pane, Word/PowerPoint show a ribbon (none present). (4) Browser identification: the top-right icon cluster is favourites star, an extension asterisk, a puzzle/extensions glyph, a split-screen glyph, profile avatar, `...` settings, and a multicoloured Copilot mark at the far right — the Edge layout. A sliver of the claude.ai conversation panel (list icon, an `×`, a partially visible label) is pinned at the far left edge of frames 001–008, confirming the artifact is open beside a chat.

palette: Page background — warm ivory / unbleached-paper cream, as photographed roughly #F3EDE1; the phone's white balance is warm-shifted against a dark room, so the true CSS value is most likely a touch lighter and less yellow, in the #F8F4EC – #FAF7F0 band. It is uniform across the full bleed, header included — the header is not a separate tint.
Primary ink (H1, H2, wordmark) — very dark desaturated slate with a cool green-blue cast, roughly #24303A photographed; true value likely ~#1F2A33 / #22303B. Notably NOT pure black.

Body / paragraph grey — warm medium grey, roughly #55585A photographed, likely ~#4A4E52 true. Clearly lighter than the headings; the contrast step between heading ink and body grey is one of the page's main hierarchy devices.
Sub-line / placeholder grey — lighter still, roughly #7C7A74, used for "Izmir Institute of Technology, Izmir, Turkey" and for the bracketed italic placeholders.

Accent terracotta / brick red — the only saturated colour on the page, used exclusively for the small outlined icons (building, envelope, map pin, chain link), roughly #A03A30 photographed; true value likely ~#9B3B32 / #A23C33. It is never used for text, buttons or rules — purely an icon accent.
Hairline rules and the hamburger button border — very light warm taupe, roughly #DED7C8 photographed, likely ~#E3DCCE. Approximately 1 px, low contrast, visible but never assertive.
Contrast-check note: heading ink on ivory is a very high-contrast pairing (~12:1); the placeholder grey on ivory is the weakest pairing on the page and is borderline for small italic text.
design.typography: Two families, cleanly split by role. HEADINGS + WORDMARK: a transitional/old-style serif with moderate-to-high stroke contrast and sharp bracketed serifs — double-storey 'g' in "Kaynardag", a 'W' with crossing middle strokes in "Where", a ball-ish terminal on the 'C' of "Contact". Regular weight, no bold; letter-spacing normal to very slightly open. Reads as Source Serif 4 / Lora / Spectral family territory (Georgia-like but finer); it is definitely not Times New Roman and not a slab. Sizes: H1 "Contact" ≈ 52–56 px, H2 "Where to find me" / "Elsewhere" ≈ 30–34 px, header wordmark ≈ 15–16 px with a hint of extra tracking. BODY: a neutral humanist sans with a tall x-height, double-storey 'a', straight-tailed 'y' and fairly open apertures — Inter / Söhne / system-ui territory. Lead paragraph ≈ 19–20 px at line-height ≈ 1.7 (measured gap between the two wrapped lines is generous). Contact-row labels ≈ 16 px semibold/600; sub-lines ≈ 15 px regular. Placeholder text is set in ITALIC sans inside square brackets — "[Email address coming soon]", "[Office details coming soon]" — the italic is load-bearing, it is what marks them as provisional. Em dashes are used as real em dashes with spaces around them ("this site — especially", "Google Scholar — link coming soon").
design.layout: Single left-aligned content column, no centring, no cards. Left gutter ≈ 4–5 % of viewport width; text wraps at ≈ 78 % of viewport width, implying a container max-width in the 1000–1100 px range at this (wide, desktop) preview viewport, with the right third of the column deliberately left empty — the page breathes rather than filling the screen. Vertical rhythm is loose and editorial: ~90 px from header to H1, ~20 px H1 to lead paragraph, ~110 px paragraph to the hairline rule, ~60 px rule to the next H2, ~28–30 px between contact rows, ~110 px between the end of a section and the next H2, ~40 px H2 to its intro line. Header is sticky/fixed at ~56–64 px tall and never scrolls. Contact rows are icon-gutter + text-stack (icon column ≈ 24 px wide, ~14 px gap to the text). The Elsewhere links are a single horizontal row of three, roughly evenly spaced across the left ~72 % of the container.
design.navigation: This is the clip's biggest open question. NO left sidebar is present in any of the 15 frames. Navigation is collapsed to a single hamburger button pinned to the TOP-RIGHT of the sticky header — a ~40 × 40 px square with a 1 px warm-taupe border, ~6–8 px corner radius, and three ~2 px dark bars. It is never clicked in this clip, so the drawer's contents, direction and animation are unknown. The sticky header's only other element is the wordmark "Korkut Kaynardag, PhD" at the left, which is presumably the home link (no hover state is captured to confirm). The route `/contact` is exposed by the Claude toolbar, not by the page, so the site's own URL scheme is path-based per page. No breadcrumb, no in-page table of contents, no footer nav, no active-state indicator is visible anywhere. Because the professor's stated requirement is "there will always be a menu on the left", this frame set shows either (a) the preview rendered below the sidebar breakpoint so the nav collapsed, or (b) a Contact page that simply has not had the left rail applied. Do not treat the hamburger-only header as the approved desktop nav.
components: Sticky header bar — full-bleed, same ivory as the page, ~56–64 px tall, 1 px #DED7C8 bottom hairline, wordmark left / hamburger right, no shadow and no background change on scroll (content slides under it cleanly).
Hamburger button — ~40 × 40 px square, 1 px warm-taupe border, ~6–8 px radius, transparent fill, three dark 2 px bars. The only button-shaped element on the page.
H1 page-title block — oversized serif heading immediately followed by a sans lead paragraph, no eyebrow/kicker, no subtitle rule.
Horizontal hairline divider — 1 px, ~#DED7C8, spanning the full content container width, used once to separate the lead paragraph from the first section. It is the page's only structural divider.
Section heading (h2) — serif, ~30–34 px, no rule beneath it, no number, no accent bar.

Contact detail row — small outlined terracotta icon in a fixed left gutter + a text stack of bold 16 px sans label over a 15 px lighter sub-line. Three variants seen: building icon (Department of Civil Engineering), envelope icon (Email), map-pin icon (Office). No card, no border, no background fill, no hover affordance visible.
Placeholder sub-line — italic sans in square brackets, in the lightest grey. Used as the explicit 'not filled in yet' convention throughout.

Inert profile link row — a three-across horizontal row of chain-link icon + label, each reading "<Service> — link coming soon", rendered in body grey with no underline and no link colour, i.e. styled as disabled/pending rather than as anchors.

NOT present on this page (worth recording as negative evidence): no cards, no pills or badges, no tables, no callout boxes, no buttons other than the hamburger, no images or figures, no footer, no back-to-top, no dark-mode toggle.
design.texture_and_effects: The ivory field carries a fine, regular VERTICAL striping across the entire screen area. Read with care: this pattern also runs over the dark browser chrome and the toolbar, which means it is overwhelmingly likely to be moire from the phone camera sampling the ViewSonic panel's subpixel grid, NOT a CSS texture. I would not rebuild a vertical linen overlay on this evidence alone. What IS attributable to the design: a flat, completely untextured ivory fill with no gradient, no vignette, no noise layer and no paper grain that survives the moire; zero box-shadows anywhere (the sticky header casts none even with content scrolling beneath it); no border-radius on any surface except the hamburger button; no rounded content cards. Motion: exactly one transition is captured — a single fast scroll between frames 008 and 009, which is a plain native scroll (frame 009 shows rolling-shutter ghosting of the moving text while the sticky header stays perfectly sharp). There is no scroll-triggered fade-in, no parallax, no reveal animation on the sections as they enter the viewport, and no visible easing overshoot. The page's visual character comes entirely from the serif/sans pairing, the ink-to-grey contrast step and the generous whitespace — not from effects.

notable: The artifact is called **Korkut's Research Hub** and is a MULTI-PAGE artifact with real routing — the Claude toolbar shows a route picker currently on `/contact` with a chevron for switching. The rebuild should keep path-based routes (`/contact`, and by implication `/research`, `/teaching`, etc.), not anchor-scrolling on one long page.

The header is genuinely STICKY, not merely at the top: across the frame-008→009 scroll the wordmark and hamburger hold at identical y while body text slides beneath them, and the header casts no shadow and gains no background tint on scroll. Reproduce as `position: sticky; top: 0` with a static background and a persistent 1 px bottom hairline.

The whole page uses exactly ONE saturated colour — the terracotta/brick red (~#9B3B32) — and only ever on 20 px line icons. Headings, body, rules and even the 'links' are all neutral. That restraint is the design's signature; adding a coloured link state or a coloured button would break it.

The serif/sans split is strict and role-based: serif for the wordmark and every heading, sans for every piece of running text and every label. There is no bold serif and no italic serif anywhere; the only italic on the page is sans, and it exclusively marks placeholder content.

The bracketed-italic `[… coming soon]` convention is used consistently as the site's placeholder idiom. When the real email and office are supplied these should drop straight into the same sub-line slot; the bracket + italic treatment should disappear with them, not be left as styling.

The content column is left-aligned with roughly a quarter of the viewport width left empty on the right. This is deliberate — text never runs edge to edge. Do not centre the column and do not widen it to fill.

Vertical rhythm is unusually generous: ~110 px between a section's end and the next h2, ~90 px from header to H1. The page feels calm because of spacing, not because of any effect. Tightening this to a conventional ~48 px would change the character completely.

There is NO motion design on the page: no scroll reveal, no fade, no parallax, no hover animation captured. The one scroll in the clip is a plain native scroll. Nothing here asks for an animation library.

The `Upgrade` pill in the toolbar means the account viewing this is on a plan where publishing may be limited — relevant if anyone tries to recover the original artifact from `project:34000a66-3304-4430-a914-5c4a1656cce7`.

The conversation is titled "Build webpage with provided files", which corroborates the professor's statement that content and figures were prepared in advance and handed to Claude — the artifact is a build from supplied material, so the source content likely still exists as files in that conversation.

"Izmir" is written with a plain ASCII `I` in both occurrences ("Izmir Institute of Technology, Izmir, Turkey") — no Turkish dotted `İ`. Keep it as-is unless he asks otherwise; changing it silently would be an unrequested edit to his own institution's name as he wrote it.
The three Elsewhere entries are laid out as a single horizontal row of three at this width. At a narrower breakpoint they will need to stack; no evidence of that responsive state exists in this clip.

Negative evidence worth keeping: no cards, no shadows, no rounded containers, no gradients, no badges, no tables, no images on this page. If the rebuild introduces any of those on Contact, it is an addition, not a restoration.

misses.claim: "the H1 'Contact' flush to the same left gutter as the wordmark (the H1 sits ~15–20 px further right in raw pixels, which is glyph side-bearing, not a different container)"
misses.correction: Not side-bearing — the header and the content column have DIFFERENT left padding. Measured ink left edges: v06_005 wordmark 'K' x=19 vs H1 'C' x=38 (Δ19). v06_002 wordmark 'K' x=84 vs H1 'C' x=103 (Δ19), with H2 'Where' at x=109 and the row icon at x=110. The frame's rotation is only 0.76° (derived from the hairlines dropping 8 px over 600 px of x), so keystone contributes <2 px over that 145 px of y, and side bearing on a 61 px 'C' vs a 27 px 'K' accounts for at most 3–4 px. Net: the wordmark hangs ~15–16 photo px (~11 CSS px) LEFT of the content column. Reproduce it deliberately or fix it — but do not describe them as aligned.

misses.claim: H1 ≈ 52–56 px; H2 ≈ 30–34 px; header wordmark ≈ 15–16 px
misses.correction: The H1 is much smaller relative to everything else than claimed. Cap heights in v06_005 (one frame, one scale): H1 'C' 41 px, H2 'W' 28 px, sans label 'E' (Email) 17 px, subline 'I' (Izmir) 16 px, lead 'F' 21 px, wordmark 'K' 18 px. Converting with serif cap 0.67em / sans cap 0.727em and anchoring the label at 1rem=16px gives H1 ≈ 42 px, H2 ≈ 28–29 px, lead ≈ 20 px, subline ≈ 15 px, wordmark ≈ 18 px. Cross-checked in v06_002 (H1 'Contact' box h=40, H2 'Where' box h=30). So H1/H2 ≈ 1.43 and H1/body ≈ 2.1 — the first pass's numbers imply 1.6–1.7 and 2.8. Its body sizes (19–20 / 16 / 15) are right; its H1 is ~30% too big and its wordmark ~15% too small.

misses.claim: "HEADINGS + WORDMARK: … Regular weight, no bold" and "There is no bold serif … anywhere"
misses.correction: The wordmark is bold or semibold. Dark-run widths through the x-height in v06_005: wordmark line 4 px runs at cap 18 (stem/cap = 0.22); H1 5–7 px at cap 41 (0.146); H2 4–6 px at cap 28 (0.179); regular sans subline 2–3 px at cap 16 (0.156). The wordmark is 40% heavier than a regular sans of the same size, and heavier than the 600-weight sans label (3–4 px at cap 17 = 0.206). Blur inflates small type, but not by that margin relative to same-size neighbours. Treat the wordmark as serif 600–700; the H1/H2 do read as 400.

misses.claim: "A faint full-container hairline rule sits ~110 px below the paragraph" and "~110 px between the end of a section and the next h2"
misses.correction: Both gaps are roughly half that. v06_005: lead line-2 ink bottom y=503, rule detected at y=565 → 62 photo px ≈ 42 CSS px. v06_015: Office placeholder bottom ≈ y=635, 'Elsewhere' cap top y=728 → 93 photo px ≈ 64 CSS px. The rule→H2 gap IS ~57 CSS px (first pass's "~60" is right). So the vertical rhythm is 2.5–4rem, i.e. generous but conventional — the claim that "tightening this to a conventional ~48 px would change the character completely" is built on a number that was never there.

misses.claim: "~90 px of empty ivory, then the H1" and "~20 px gap" from H1 to the lead paragraph
misses.correction: v06_005: header hairline y≈252 → H1 cap top y=345 = 93 photo px ≈ 64 CSS px (not 90). H1 ink bottom y=387 → lead cap top y=435 = 48 photo px ≈ 33 CSS px (not 20). Header height itself: v06_010 panel top y≈150 → hairline y=248 = 98 photo px ≈ 67 CSS px, slightly above the claimed 56–64.

misses.claim: "Left gutter ≈ 4–5 % of viewport width" / "the page breathes rather than filling the screen"
misses.correction: The left gutter is tight in absolute terms. In v06_002 the preview panel's left edge is at x≈67 (row scans at y=670 and y=745 jump 60→164→184 between x=64 and x=70) and the H1 ink starts at x=103 → ~33 photo px ≈ 23–28 CSS px, about 2.5% of the ≥1110 px viewport, not 4–5%. The header's own gutter is smaller still (~16 photo px ≈ 11 CSS px). Content is hard against the left edge; the breathing room is on the RIGHT, not symmetric.

misses.claim: "the content container is left-aligned with a max-width of roughly 1000–1100 px" / the divider spans "the full content container width" (i.e. same width as the text)
misses.correction: The rules are much wider than the prose. Tracing the mid-page rule across x in v06_002 it is absent at x=80–100 and present from x≈120 onward (depths 2.7→5.9), i.e. it starts at the container edge (H1 left = 103), and in v06_005/006/008 it is still detected strongly at x=1600 (depth 3.9–6.9 in the text-free strip x1400–1600). The lead paragraph, by contrast, ends at x=1289 in v06_005. So: a full-width (unclamped) container carrying the header hairline and the <hr>, with the PROSE capped ~250–300 CSS px narrower (~860–890 px, ≈95 characters per line). Rebuilding it as one 1000–1100 px column would shorten the rules and lengthen nothing.

misses.claim: the hamburger is "at the far right (x≈1610 of a 1664-wide frame, i.e. hard against the viewport's right edge)"
misses.correction: Unsupported — the viewport is cropped by the frame, not ending at it. Row y=400 sampled at x=1600…1663 returns flat page ivory in v06_002 (175→169), v06_005 (176→172) and v06_011 (168→166); there is no edge. The Publish pill is clipped in most frames and only just fits in v06_004, so the window right edge is ~1680–1700 photo px. Measured button box right edge is x≈1645–1647, leaving ~35–55 photo px (~25–38 CSS px) of page to its right. Nothing in this clip establishes the viewport width, so "text wraps at ≈78% of viewport width" is also unmeasurable here.

misses.claim: "Hamburger button — ~40 × 40 px square… three dark 2 px bars" (and implicitly aligned with the wordmark)

Border columns/rows: v06_004 x1576…1645, y187…252 (69×65); v06_012 x1578…1647, y151…215 (69×64) → ~46×43 CSS px, not 40×40. Bars: three, equal length, x1600…1626 (≈18 CSS px wide), pitch 10 photo px (≈7 CSS px), thickness ~3–4 photo px (~2 CSS px) — the 2 px bars are right. Alignment: v06_004 box centre y=219.5 vs wordmark box y225…250 (cap centre ≈234); v06_012 box centre y=183 vs wordmark y187…214 (cap centre ≈197). The button sits ~15–18 photo px (~10–12 CSS px) ABOVE the wordmark's optical centre in both — the header is not `align-items: center`.

misses.claim: "Accent terracotta / brick red… roughly #A03A30 photographed; true value likely ~#9B3B32 / #A23C33" — repeated as the design's signature
misses.correction: The accent is a dusty ROSE / muted crimson, not a terracotta. Terracotta requires B < G; every icon measures B ≈ G or B > G once you remove the scene's warm cast. v06_011 at matched luminance: building icon (124.9, 104.1, 103.6) → R−G=+20.8, G−B=+0.5, vs the adjacent 'Department' label (106.9, 101.4, 91.9) → R−G=+5.5, G−B=+9.5. Same pattern in v06_005 for all three glyphs (building 116.4/99.3/95.0, envelope 113.3/104.8/96.6, map-pin 113.6/101.9/95.6) and in v06_013 for the chain-link glyph. White-balancing on the ivory in linear light lands the stroke at R > B > G (hue ≈ 340–350°). Blur toward a warm ivory background would bias this TOWARD terracotta, so the true colour is at least this cool. A 2× magnified crop of v06_010 reads visibly mauve/old-rose. Caveat: 4:2:0 chroma subsampling degrades hue on thin strokes — worth one screenshot to confirm — but do not build in #9B3B32 on this evidence.

misses.claim: the three Elsewhere entries are "rendered in the muted body grey"
misses.correction: They are a tier lighter AND a step smaller than body copy. v06_015, same frame, same glare: 'My academic profiles and CV will be linked here.' darkest-3% = (99.2, 95.6, 89.3), ascender-to-descender box h=23; 'Google Scholar — link coming soon' = (117.9, 112.8, 106.8), h=21. v06_013 agrees (intro 95.9/91.3/82.9 vs link 118.5/113.3/108.2). So the pending links sit in the SAME lightest tier as the `[… coming soon]` placeholders (v06_005 placeholder 124.0/119.7/107.8, subline 119.9/115.3/104.0), at roughly 0.9rem. That is the point of the treatment — they match the placeholder idiom, they are not body text that merely lost its link colour.

misses.claim: "a single horizontal row (flex/3-column grid) at roughly x≈65, x≈510, x≈890 … wide, roughly even gutters"
misses.correction: Equal GAPS, unequal columns — it is content-sized flex, not a 3-column grid. v06_015: item1 x54…437, item2 x499…820, item3 x881…1267. critics.confidence_in_first_pass: Moderate. The structural and qualitative reads hold up and I confirmed them independently: it is the Contact page inside a Claude artifact preview in Edge; the transcription is complete and correct; the header genuinely is sticky AND opaque; there is exactly one accent colour and it is used only on icons; the serif/sans role split is strict; the bracketed-italic placeholder idiom is consistent; there is exactly one <hr> on the page; there are no cards, shadows, radii, gradients, badges, images or motion of any kind; the moire is camera artefact and not a CSS texture; and the navigation warning ("do not treat the hamburger-only header as the approved desktop nav") is not only right but understated, since I can show the sidebar is still absent at ≥1110 CSS px. What is unreliable is almost every NUMBER. Most spacing figures are photo pixels presented as CSS pixels, and two of them (the "~110 px" gaps it built its "unusually generous rhythm" thesis on) are wrong by 2.5× even in photo pixels. The H1 size is ~30% too large and the wordmark ~15% too small and wrongly called regular weight when it measures bold. Three claims are confidently asserted from evidence the frames do not contain: that the wordmark and H1 share a gutter (they differ by a consistent 19 photo px in two independent frames), that the hamburger is flush to the viewport's right edge (the viewport runs past the frame crop in every frame), and that the container max-width is 1000–1100 px (the rules run ~250–300 CSS px wider than the prose). The terracotta accent is the single riskiest item — it is repeated eight times as "the design's signature" and my measurements put the hue on the rose/crimson side in three different glyphs across two frames. Net: reuse the first pass's prose and its negative evidence; re-derive every number, and get one real screenshot before committing the accent colour.
